result:
The proposed answer $2n^2+3n$ is very likely correct, though the proposal's argument has gaps for general $n$.

**Lower bound (rigorous).** For $x=\begin{pmatrix}A_1&B_1\\C_1&A_1^T\end{pmatrix}$ and $y=\begin{pmatrix}A_2&B_2\\C_2&A_2^T\end{pmatrix}$, the upper-right block of $[x,y]$ is $M=A_1B_2+B_2A_1^T$ (signs don't matter in characteristic 2). It is symmetric, and $M_{ii}=2\sum_k (A_1)_{ik}(B_2)_{ik}=0$. The same holds for the lower-left block. So $[\mathfrak{sp}_{2n},\mathfrak{sp}_{2n}]\subseteq\mathfrak{o}(q)$, which has dimension $n(2n-1)$. The commuting variety is the zero locus of the bracket map $\mathfrak{g}\times\mathfrak{g}\to\mathfrak{o}(q)$, so every component has dimension at least $2n(2n+1)-n(2n-1)=2n^2+3n$.

**$n=1$.** For $\mathfrak{sl}_2$ in characteristic 2, with $x=\begin{pmatrix}a&b\\c&a\end{pmatrix}$ and $y=\begin{pmatrix}\alpha&\beta\\\gamma&\alpha\end{pmatrix}$, one gets $[x,y]=(b\gamma+\beta c)I$. The commuting variety is a hypersurface in $k^6$, so its dimension is $5=2+3$. ✓

**$n=2$, minimal centralizer.** Take $x=\begin{pmatrix}A&0\\C&A\end{pmatrix}$ with $A=\mathrm{diag}(s,t)$, $u=s+t\neq0$, $C=\begin{pmatrix}c_1&c_2\\c_2&c_3\end{pmatrix}$, and $c_1c_3\neq0$. Writing $y=\begin{pmatrix}P&Q\\R&P^T\end{pmatrix}$ with $Q,R$ symmetric, the equations $[x,y]=0$ reduce to six independent linear conditions:
$$q_1=q_2=q_3=0,\quad P_{12}=P_{21}=0,\quad c_2(P_{11}+P_{22})+u\,r_2=0.$$
So the centralizer has dimension $10-6=4=2n$. Together with the lower bound, the minimum centralizer dimension for $\mathfrak{sp}_4$ is 4, which confirms the proposal's claim for $n=2$.

**Gaps.**
- The proposal asserts that a generic $x$ has $[x,\mathfrak{sp}_{2n}]=\mathfrak{o}(q)$ for all $n$ without proof.
- The Jacobian argument only gives the dimension of the component through a generic smooth point. It does not rule out other components or strata of $\mathcal{C}$ with larger dimension.
- The $n=2$ "construction" is stated without details. I verified it independently above.

For $n=1,2$ the formula is confirmed. For general $n$ it rests on the expected index $2n$ being the generic centralizer dimension, with no other stratum dominating. That is plausible but not shown here.

VERDICT: ACCEPT
